page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for tile and integer operations.

The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it bundles a 480 GB NVMe SSD, which is Premium Storage capable. No dedicated GPU hardware is included in this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, the L2s_v4 demonstrates strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 31.24 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show notable limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth are positioned in the lower tiers. Similarly, multi-core Geekbench scores and Passmark database operations reflect the constraints of the single physical core design.

Qualitatively, the L2s_v4 offers a specialized hardware profile that balances high-speed single-core compute with fast local NVMe storage. It is suitable for workloads that require low-latency local storage access and moderate memory capacity without demanding heavy multi-threaded CPU parallelization. Appropriate workloads include lightweight database hosting, single-threaded data processing, and basic web serving applications.
